questions.question: List the main components of the Solar System.
questions.modelAnswer: The Sun. Eight planets and their moons. Dwarf planets. Asteroids. Comets. Artificial satellites.
markingPoints: The Sun.
Eight planets and their moons.
Dwarf planets.
Asteroids.
Comets.
Artificial satellites.

questions.question: Describe how a star forms from a nebula.
questions.modelAnswer: Gravity pulls gas and dust together. The cloud collapses and forms a protostar. Gravitational energy heats it. When temperature and pressure are high enough, hydrogen fusion begins and a stable main-sequence star forms.
markingPoints: Gravity pulls gas and dust together.
The cloud collapses and forms a protostar.
Gravitational energy heats it.
When temperature and pressure are high enough, hydrogen fusion begins and a stable main-sequence star forms.

questions.question: Explain why a main-sequence star is stable.
questions.modelAnswer: Inward gravitational force is balanced by outward pressure/radiation produced by energy from nuclear fusion. The star is in equilibrium.
markingPoints: Inward gravitational force is balanced by outward pressure/radiation produced by energy from nuclear fusion.
The star is in equilibrium.

questions.question: Describe the life cycle of a star with a mass similar to the Sun.
questions.modelAnswer: Nebula → protostar → main sequence → red giant → planetary nebula → white dwarf The white dwarf eventually cools.
markingPoints: Nebula → protostar → main sequence → red giant → planetary nebula → white dwarf
The white dwarf eventually cools.

questions.question: Describe the life cycle of a star much more massive than the Sun.
questions.modelAnswer: Nebula → protostar → main sequence → red supergiant → supernova → neutron star or, for the most massive cores, black hole.
markingPoints: Nebula → protostar → main sequence → red supergiant → supernova → neutron star or, for the most massive cores, black hole.

questions.question: Explain how stars produce and distribute elements.
questions.modelAnswer: Fusion in stars makes elements up to iron. Heavier elements are produced in supernova explosions. The explosion distributes elements into space. Later stars and planets form from enriched material.
markingPoints: Fusion in stars makes elements up to iron.
Heavier elements are produced in supernova explosions.
The explosion distributes elements into space.
Later stars and planets form from enriched material.

questions.question: Explain why a planet remains in a near-circular orbit around the Sun.
questions.modelAnswer: Gravity provides a force towards the Sun. This centripetal force changes the direction of velocity. The planet continually falls towards the Sun but moves sideways fast enough to miss it.
markingPoints: Gravity provides a force towards the Sun.
This centripetal force changes the direction of velocity.
The planet continually falls towards the Sun but moves sideways fast enough to miss it.

questions.question: State the qualitative relationship between orbital radius and orbital speed for planets around the same star.
questions.modelAnswer: As orbital radius increases, orbital speed decreases.
markingPoints: As orbital radius increases, orbital speed decreases.

questions.question: Distinguish natural and artificial satellites and give one use of an artificial satellite.
questions.modelAnswer: Natural satellites orbit naturally, e.g. the Moon. Artificial satellites are human-made. Uses include communication, weather monitoring, navigation or Earth observation.
markingPoints: Natural satellites orbit naturally, e.g. the Moon.
Artificial satellites are human-made.
Uses include communication, weather monitoring, navigation or Earth observation.

questions.question: Explain red-shift in light from distant galaxies.
questions.modelAnswer: Spectral lines are shifted to longer wavelengths/lower frequencies. This occurs because galaxies are moving away. Greater red-shift indicates greater recession speed.
markingPoints: Spectral lines are shifted to longer wavelengths/lower frequencies.
This occurs because galaxies are moving away.
Greater red-shift indicates greater recession speed.

questions.question: Explain how red-shift provides evidence that the Universe is expanding.
questions.modelAnswer: Most galaxies show red-shift, so they are receding. More distant galaxies generally recede faster. This pattern is consistent with space expanding.
markingPoints: Most galaxies show red-shift, so they are receding.
More distant galaxies generally recede faster.
This pattern is consistent with space expanding.

questions.question: State two key observations supporting the Big Bang model.
questions.modelAnswer: Red-shift/recession of galaxies supports expansion. Cosmic microwave background radiation is remnant radiation from a hot early Universe.
markingPoints: Red-shift/recession of galaxies supports expansion.
Cosmic microwave background radiation is remnant radiation from a hot early Universe.

questions.question: Explain why cosmic microwave background radiation supports the Big Bang model.
questions.modelAnswer: A hot early Universe should leave background radiation. Expansion stretches and cools it into the microwave region. It is detected uniformly across space.
markingPoints: A hot early Universe should leave background radiation.
Expansion stretches and cools it into the microwave region.
It is detected uniformly across space.

questions.question: Explain why scientific models of the Universe may change.
questions.modelAnswer: New observations or improved measurements may conflict with predictions. Evidence is evaluated and replicated. Models are modified or replaced to explain the full evidence base.
markingPoints: New observations or improved measurements may conflict with predictions.
Evidence is evaluated and replicated.
Models are modified or replaced to explain the full evidence base.

questions.question: A satellite moves in a circular orbit of radius 7.0 × 10⁶ m with period 5.8 × 10³ s. Calculate its orbital speed.
questions.modelAnswer: Circumference = 2πr Distance = 2π × 7.0 × 10⁶ = 4.40 × 10⁷ m V = distance ÷ time V = 4.40 × 10⁷ ÷ 5.8 × 10³ V = 7.6 × 10³ m/s
markingPoints: Circumference = 2πr
Distance = 2π × 7.0 × 10⁶ = 4.40 × 10⁷ m
V = distance ÷ time
